title: The first Tor kernel boundary, natural in presentations
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. Use Tor as in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. For every surjective R-linear map q:F \to N, there are simultaneously chosen R-linear maps \delta_q:\operatorname{Tor}_1^R(N,M) \to \ker(q)\otimes_R M. The pairs \operatorname{Tor}_1(q,M),\delta_q and \delta_q,(\ker(q) inclusion \otimes 1_M) are exact. For every two such surjections q:F \to N and qprime:Fprime \to Nprime and R-linear maps a:F \to Fprime, b:N \to Nprime, c:\ker(q) \to \ker(qprime) with qprime a=b q and inclusion c=a inclusion, one has \delta_{qprime}\operatorname{Tor}_1(b,M)=(c\otimes 1_M)\delta_q. No grading, minimality, freeness or finite generation is assumed.

source.place: Section 00LY, Tags 00M0 (Tor exact sequence), 00LZ (resolution functoriality), 00M3 (Tor symmetry); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00LY

proof.text: For each surjection q:F -> N, the kernel inclusion is injective and its image is the kernel of q. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-resolution-ses-split] to obtain free resolutions of the three terms with split rows. Tensoring with M preserves their splitting identities. This gives a short exact sequence of tensor complexes.

Take the connecting map H_1(N resolution tensor M) -> H_0(ker(q) resolution tensor M). By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] the pairs adjacent to this map are exact. The resolution comparison [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] identifies H_1 with Tor_1 and the induced map from F with Tor_1(q,M). By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], the augmentations identify H_0 with ker(q) tensor M and F tensor M and their map with the tensor of the inclusion. Transporting the two exact pairs gives the claimed exactness, as in [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable].

A square (a,b,c) gives a morphism of short exact kernel sequences. Lift this to a chain ladder between the horseshoe resolutions: starting at degree zero, lift the free right terms along the surjective target augmentation, correct the middle lift by a map into the left terms, and repeat on the kernel sequences. The degreewise split rows and projectivity of the source free terms supply the required lifts; their differentials are inclusions after the kernel surjections, so the inductively lifted maps commute with the differentials. Tensor this ladder with M. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] its maps commute with the homology boundary. Explicitly, a cycle z lifts to y in the middle tensor complex and d y is the image of a kernel element w; the images of y and w are admissible choices for the image cycle. Independence of choices and resolution comparison [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] identify this square with delta_qprime Tor_1(b,M)=(c tensor 1_M) delta_q. It works for the initially chosen resolution of each sequence; hence the choices give the simultaneous natural family.

proof_origin.place: Section 00LY, Tags 00M0 (Tor exact sequence), 00LZ (resolution functoriality), 00M3 (Tor symmetry); https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00LY
proof_origin.note: First-variable horseshoe and cycle naturality argument expanded from the cited sources.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_tor_kernel_boundary_natural
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{u} R) :
    ∃ δ : ∀ (F N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (q : F →ₗ[R] N),
        Function.Surjective q →
          (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj N).obj M) →ₗ[R]
            (LinearMap.ker q ⊗[R] M),
      (∀ (F N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (q : F →ₗ[R] N) (hq : Function.Surjective q),
        Function.Exact (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).map
          (ModuleCat.ofHom q)).app M).hom (δ F N q hq) ∧
        Function.Exact (δ F N q hq) ((LinearMap.ker q).subtype.rTensor M)) ∧
      (∀ (F N F' N' : ModuleCat.{u} R) (q : F →ₗ[R] N) (q' : F' →ₗ[R] N')
          (hq : Function.Surjective q) (hq' : Function.Surjective q')
          (a : F →ₗ[R] F') (b : N →ₗ[R] N')
          (c : LinearMap.ker q →ₗ[R] LinearMap.ker q'),
        q'.comp a = b.comp q →
        (∀ x : LinearMap.ker q, (c x : F') = a (x : F)) →
        ∀ t : (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).obj N).obj M),
          δ F' N' q' hq' ((((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) 1).map
            (ModuleCat.ofHom b)).app M).hom t) =
          c.rTensor M (δ F N q hq t))
